summary.title: Influence of plant growth regulators and nitrogen sources on the production and development of Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk Hormonal treatment and fertilization to plant development
summary.authors: Leone Campos Rocha; Fábio Andrade; Teixeira; Márcio Dos; Santos Pedreira; Daniela Deitos Fries; Giovanna Evely; Leite Costa; Ana Cláudia; Maia Soares; Daniel Lucas; Santos Dias; Abdias José De Figueiredo; Angel Amaral; Seixas; Camile Carvalho Pacheco
summary.executive_summary: This study evaluated the effects of seed treatment with plant growth regulators (PGR) and nitrogen fertilization methods on the growth and development of Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk. The research aimed to optimize pasture establishment by analyzing germination characteristics, dry matter yield, and physiological composition. Two experiments were conducted: one focusing on germination and initial growth at 30 days after sowing (DAS), and another on dry mass production and pigment content under different fertilization regimes. The PGR used was a mixture of auxin, cytokinin, and gibberellin. Results indicated that PGR treatment increased germination percentages and root dry mass, with optimal levels estimated at 10.3 mL.kg-1 for germination and 12.8 mL.kg-1 for root mass. A significant interaction was found between seed type (coated vs. conventional) and PGR levels for leaf and pseudostem dry mass, where coated seeds performed better at lower PGR concentrations. In the second experiment, soil nitrogen fertilization resulted in higher dry mass productions of leaf, stem, shoot, and root compared to foliar or no fertilization. The combination of PGR and soil fertilization yielded the highest dry mass for stem, leaf, and shoot. PGR also increased chlorophyll a content, suggesting enhanced photosynthetic efficiency. The study concludes that exogenous hormonal compounds act on organogenesis and increase development, while soil N-fertilization maximizes photosynthetic processes and growth rates. Lower PGR levels are recommended for coated seeds due to their higher embryo quality and protection.

claims.description: Plant growth regulators increase germination and root dry mass in Brachiaria decumbens.
Soil nitrogen fertilization is more effective than foliar fertilization for dry mass production.
Coated seeds perform better at lower PGR levels than conventional seeds.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study evaluated the effects of seed treatment with plant growth regulators (PGR) and nitrogen fertilization methods on the growth and development of Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk. The research aimed to optimize pasture establishment by analyzing germination characteristics, dry matter yield, and physiological composition. Two experiments were conducted: one focusing on germination and initial growth at 30 days after sowing (DAS), and another on dry mass production and pigment content under different fertilization regimes. The PGR used was a mixture of auxin, cytokinin, and gibberellin. Results indicated that PGR treatment increased germination percentages and root dry mass, with optimal levels estimated at 10.3 mL.kg-1 for germination and 12.8 mL.kg-1 for root mass. A significant interaction was found between seed type (coated vs. conventional) and PGR levels for leaf and pseudostem dry mass, where coated seeds performed better at lower PGR concentrations. In the second experiment, soil nitrogen fertilization resulted in higher dry mass productions of leaf, stem, shoot, and root compared to foliar or no fertilization. The combination of PGR and soil fertilization yielded the highest dry mass for stem, leaf, and shoot. PGR also increased chlorophyll a content, suggesting enhanced photosynthetic efficiency. The study concludes that exogenous hormonal compounds act on organogenesis and increase development, while soil N-fertilization maximizes photosynthetic processes and growth rates. Lower PGR levels are recommended for coated seeds due to their higher embryo quality and protection.

Research Context
Adverse climatic factors shorten the soil preparation and planting window. This reduction necessitates greater seed efficiency in germination and emergence speed. Management practices are essential to improve herbage production using favorable climatic conditions. Synthetic compounds act as growth promoters with effects similar to phytohormones. Phytohormones regulate homeostasis through signaling networks and intermediary metabolites. High levels of gibberellic compounds are uneconomical and reduce forage mass. Low concentrations of gibberellin positively affect forage yield. PGRs show potential under stress by regulating growth-related genes. Nitrogen expands the plant lifecycle and increases vegetative growth rates. Increased photoassimilate production maximizes structural characteristics and post-defoliation recovery. Nitrogen is an indispensable constituent in organic compounds and cell division. Nitrogen applications to degraded pastures increase water use efficiency and soil cover.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The aim was to evaluate the effect of seed treatment with PGR and nitrogen fertilization. The study focused on Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk growth and development. Germinative characteristics were assessed as a primary outcome. Dry matter yield was a key metric for evaluating growth. Physiological composition, including pigments, was analyzed to assess health. It was hypothesized that PGR would increase germination and mass yields. It was expected that soil N-fertilization would increase dry mass productions. The interaction between seed type and PGR levels was a specific focus. Coated seeds were hypothesized to perform better at lower PGR levels. Embryo quality was expected to contribute to greater tissue formation. Soil fertilization was predicted to maximize photosynthetic processes. Exogenous hormonal compounds were expected to act on organogenesis.

Methodological Details
Experiments were performed at UESB, Itapetinga-BA, between June and September 2017. Germination was conducted in a Mangelsdorf germination chamber (MA-401). Germination conditions included a 12h photoperiod and constant 28ºC temperature. Growth evaluations were performed in a greenhouse using pots with 12 kg dry soil. Soil was collected at 0-20 cm depth and passed through a 4-mm sieve. Fertilization recommendations were based on the Soil Fertility Commission for Minas Gerais. A 2 x 4 factorial scheme in a completely randomized design (CRD) was used. Two commercial seed types (coated and conventional) were tested. Four levels of growth regulator (0, 8, 16, 24 mL.kg-1) were applied. Seeds were imbibed in PGR for approximately two hours. The PGR contained auxin (0.05 mg.L-1), cytokinin (0.09 mg.L-1), and gibberellin (0.05 mg.L-1). Initial growth assessments were done at 30 days after sowing (DAS). Sowing was performed in seedling trays with 32 cells per replicate. Sterilized coconut residue was used as the substrate for initial growth. The second experiment evaluated PGR (0, 24 mL.kg-1) and four nitrogen fertilization methods. Eight treatments were used with four plants per replicate and four replicates. A standardization cut was performed at 30 DAS with a 15 cm residue height. Data collection followed two periods of 28 days after the cut. Soil and foliar nitrogen fertilization rates were 75 kg.ha-1 N and 3 L.ha-1. Data were analyzed using the MIXED procedure of SAS. Significance was declared when P ≤ 0.05. Germination percentage and speed index (GSI) were determined over 14 days. Chlorophylls and carotenoids were quantified using DMSO extraction and spectrophotometry.

Procedures And Architectures
Germination was monitored daily for 14 days to determine percentage and GSI. Whole-plant yield was determined at the end of the experimental period. Fresh and dry mass of root, stem, and leaf were measured. The third fully expanded leaf was collected at 10 a.m. for pigment analysis. An aliquot of 200 mg fresh mass was prepared for pigment extraction. 5 mL of DMSO was added to the leaf aliquot for extraction. Readings were taken at wavelengths of 665, 649, and 480 nm. Pigment values were adjusted to mg.g-1 of fresh mass. Regression equations were used to estimate maximum points for PGR effects. Tukey test was used for comparison of means in Experiment 2. Single-degree-of-freedom contrast statements analyzed linear and quadratic PGR effects. Seed, PGR, and interaction effects were analyzed as fixed effects. The foliar fertilizer composition included N, P2O5, Mg, S, Zn, Mn, Cu, B, Mo, Co. The density of the foliar spray was 1.37 g.mL-1. Soil fertilization was applied after the standardization cut. Foliar fertilization was applied as a spray. Multiple fertilization combined soil and foliar methods. Greenhouse temperature and humidity were recorded using a digital thermo-hygrometer.

Key Results
The interaction between seed type and PGR levels was not significant for germination. There was a quadratic effect of PGR levels on germination. Treatment with 10.3 mL.kg-1 PGR promoted greater germination. Coated seeds had higher germination values than conventional seeds. Treatment with 12.8 mL.kg-1 PGR resulted in higher root dry mass. There was an interaction between seed type and PGR for leaf and pseudostem mass. Coated seeds performed better at 8.85 mL.kg-1 for leaf mass. Coated seeds performed better at 9.57 mL.kg-1 for pseudostem mass. Conventional seeds required 15.5 mL.kg-1 for leaf mass. Conventional seeds required 18.1 mL.kg-1 for pseudostem mass. Soil fertilization resulted in higher dry mass of leaf, stem, shoot, and root. Combining PGR and soil fertilization yielded the greatest stem, leaf, and shoot mass. PGR reduced leaf, stem, and shoot production when combined with multiple fertilization. PGR increased root dry mass only when combined with multiple fertilization. PGR had a significant effect on chlorophyll a content. Fertilization methods influenced levels of chlorophyll a, b, and carotenoids.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Exogenous hormones change hormonal balance and biosynthesis levels. Increased gibberellin concentration implies greater intracellular transport of metabolites. Gibberellin acts on genes responsible for germinative characteristics. Gibberellin reduces abscisic acid concentrations, overcoming dormancy. Coated seeds have higher germination due to protection and nutrient provision. Auxin in PGR increases rhizogenesis by stimulating stem cell multiplication. PIN proteins enable intracellular transport of auxins. Conventional seeds require higher PGR levels due to reduced efficiency. Hormonal interactions are comprised of a signaling network. Soil fertilization is more efficient for photosynthetic processes than foliar. Combined PGR and soil fertilization reflect in higher dry mass accumulation. Higher chlorophyll a levels favor ATP synthesis in chloroplasts. Foliar nitrogen may participate in cytokinin synthesis and chlorophyll production.

Claims
Plant growth regulators increase germination and root dry mass in Brachiaria decumbens. PGR increased germination percentages for both seed types. Optimal PGR level for germination was 10.3 mL.kg-1. Optimal PGR level for root mass was 12.8 mL.kg-1. Some studies found no significant response to specific hormone sets. PGR is a key tool in pasture establishment.
Soil nitrogen fertilization is more effective than foliar fertilization for dry mass production. Soil fertilization resulted in higher dry mass of all structures. Combining PGR and soil fertilization yielded the greatest mass. PGR reduced mass when combined with multiple fertilization. Soil N-fertilization maximizes photosynthetic processes and growth rates.
Coated seeds perform better at lower PGR levels than conventional seeds. Coated seeds had higher germination and GSI. Coated seeds performed better at 8.85 mL.kg-1 for leaf mass. Conventional seeds required higher PGR levels for optimal mass. Lower PGR levels are recommended for coated seeds.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Regression equations were used to estimate maximum points for PGR effects. Tukey test was used for comparison of means. Single-degree-of-freedom contrast statements analyzed PGR effects.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows average, minimum, and maximum temperatures and relative humidity. Table 1 describes the composition of the foliar spray. Table 2 presents germination characteristics for different seed types. Table 3 shows root dry mass production. Table 4 details leaf and pseudostem dry mass production. Table 5 presents dry mass production under different fertilization methods. Table 6 shows contents of chlorophylls and carotenoids.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the evaluation of PGR and nitrogen fertilization effects on Brachiaria decumbens. 2. The strongest evidence is the significant increase in dry mass with soil fertilization and PGR. 3. The future path involves optimizing PGR levels for different seed types.
